findings.source_passage: A pale, death-glimmer lit up Fedallah's sunken eyes; a hideous motion gnawed his mouth.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after 'shooting to leeward; and Ahab heading the onset'
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is a critically distinctive, rhetorically unique characterization of Fedallah at the moment of the chase's onset — it carries heavy interpretive weight about his foreknowledge and demonic nature, and is stylistically signature (the pairing of 'death-glimmer' with 'hideous motion gnawed').
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'A pale, death-glimmer lit up Fedallah's sunken eyes; a hideous motion gnawed his mouth.' immediately after the boats are dropped and Ahab leads the onset.

findings.source_passage: the sum total of those shallow pains kindly diffused through feebler men's whole lives... those noble natures contain the entire circumferences of inferior souls.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'But this intensity of his physical prostration'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most critically discussed philosophical passages in the chapter — the meditation on heroic suffering versus ordinary suffering and the 'entire circumferences of inferior souls' formulation is central to readings of Ahab's tragic magnitude. The draft keeps only the first clause and excises the full argument.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full philosophical passage: 'great hearts sometimes condense to one deep pang, the sum total of those shallow pains kindly diffused through feebler men's whole lives. And so, such hearts, though summary in each one suffering; still, if the gods decree it, in their life-time aggregate a whole age of woe... those noble natures contain the entire circumferences of inferior souls.'

findings.source_passage: he gazed beyond the whale's place, towards the dim blue spaces and wide wooing vacancies to leeward.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Dim blue spaces and wide wooing vacancies' is one of the chapter's most poetically distinctive phrases, establishing Ahab's momentary yielding to existential vastness; its absence flattens the psychological and lyrical register of this pause.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: after 'An hour,' said Ahab, include 'he gazed beyond the whale's place, towards the dim blue spaces and wide wooing vacancies to leeward' before the breeze freshens.

findings.source_passage: so planetarily swift the ever-contracting circles he made... whose centre had now become the old man's head.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'For so revolvingly appalling was the White Whale's aspect'
findings.why_it_matters: 'Planetarily swift' and 'whose centre had now become the old man's head' are prosodically and rhetorically distinctive — the cosmic scale of 'planetarily' and the geometric horror of 'centre' are signature Melville. The draft reduces this to 'contracting circles' without the voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the rhetorical force: 'so revolvingly appalling was the White Whale's aspect, and so planetarily swift the ever-contracting circles he made... whose centre had now become the old man's head.'

findings.source_passage: Fedallah incuriously and mildly eyed him; the clinging crew, at the other drifting end, could not succor him
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Meantime, from the beginning all this...' preceded by Ahab in the foam
findings.why_it_matters: Fedallah's cold, incurious gaze at the drowning Ahab is interpretively loaded — it signals his demonic detachment and foreshadows his prophecy's fulfillment. Its omission removes a key characterization beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Fedallah's reaction: 'Fedallah incuriously and mildly eyed him' as Ahab bobs helpless in the foam.

findings.source_passage: as desolate sounds from out ravines
findings.why_it_matters: 'As desolate sounds from out ravines' completes the simile and is the distinctive, strange phrase that makes the passage memorable; 'nameless wails' without the ravines comparison loses its wild geographical displacement.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full simile: 'Far inland, nameless wails came from him, as desolate sounds from out ravines.'

findings.source_passage: as in an already over-clouded sky fresh troops of clouds will sometimes sail across, so over the old man's face there now stole some such added gloom as this.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'As he was thus walking, uttering no sound'
findings.why_it_matters: This atmospheric simile describes Ahab's expression as he pauses before the wrecked boat and is voice-distinctive; its removal flattens the moment to bare action.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the cloud-simile when Ahab pauses at the wrecked boat: 'as in an already over-clouded sky fresh troops of clouds will sometimes sail across, so over the old man's face there now stole some such added gloom as this.'

summary: The draft omits two high-severity signatures (Fedallah's death-glimmer and the full noble-natures philosophical passage) and flattens three further medium-severity passages (the 'wide wooing vacancies,' 'planetarily swift,' and Fedallah's incurious gaze), making regeneration necessary.
